$comment: W-4 (I-3) — reviewed exception register for the service-client principal check.
Enforced by web/scripts/checkServiceClientPrincipal.mjs; locked by web/tests/access/serviceClientPrincipalCheck.test.ts.
Three lists, three different meanings. Do not merge them.
exceptions — a route with a VERIFIED orthogonal authorization model. Reviewed and permanent.
Adding one is a security decision: name the model and cite the line that enforces it.
baseline   — a route with NO verified model. Real W-15 remediation work, frozen 2026-07-31.
FROZEN: entries may be removed as they are fixed, never added.
advisory_transitive_only — reaches a service client through a helper rather than importing one,
so it is outside the enforced predicate. Listed so the set cannot grow silently.
All three lists may only shrink. A stale entry fails the check.
The `ratchet` ceilings below are ENFORCED BY THE CHECK, not only by the lock. Over the
ceiling is a violation; under it is stale, because a ceiling left above a fallen floor hands
out that many free exceptions. All three must be re-tightened whenever the floor moves.
`max_baseline` is the freeze clause as a ceiling, seeded at 0. The check ALSO enforces that
every exception names a `model` and a `reason`, that every baseline entry states
`why_not_an_exception` and a `w15_note`, and that the two lists are disjoint — so an entry
cannot be stripped of its review and stay green. Before 2026-09-06 those clauses lived only
in the vitest lock, which no CI workflow runs.
CITATION CONVENTION: backtick the SYMBOL beside every line number (`fnName` at `:73`), never
a bare number. A bare number cannot be checked by a human or a tool, which is why drift here
recurred three times before anyone measured it.
CONVENTION FULLY APPLIED 2026-09-06 (eighth issuance). Every exception entry that carries a
line reference now binds a symbol to it, and every reference was re-derived against the tree
rather than copied forward. Of the entries audited that pass, 2 carried SUBSTANTIVE errors —
`action/[token]` named an `.eq("token", …)` that exists nowhere in the repo, and
`public/forms/[token]/resolve` named a gate symbol that is neither imported nor called in the
route — and 6 more line references had drifted. NOTHING here changed a route, a list
membership or a count; the authorization models were re-verified and all hold.

exceptions.reason: Read-only action-link metadata. The row is selected BY the bearer token — `.from("action_links")` at `:21`, `.eq("token_hash", hashFormLinkToken(token))` at `:23` — so the token is the authorization, per I-4. No caller-supplied row selector. CITATIONS CORRECTED 2026-09-06 (eighth issuance), and this one was SUBSTANTIVE: the entry claimed the selector was `.eq("token", token)` at `:22`. Line `:22` is the `.select(...)`, and no `.eq("token", …)` exists on this route or on any of the four sibling action-link routes — all five select by `token_hash`. The real model is STRONGER than the one the register described (the column stores a SHA, so a database read cannot recover a bearer token), but a reason that names a call which is not in the file cannot be checked by anyone, and a reader reconciling code to register could have `fixed` the code toward the weaker form.

Row selected by the bearer token — `.from("action_links")` at `:17`, `.eq("token_hash", hashFormLinkToken(token))` at `:19`. Expiry and single-use are checked and return 410 (verified by phase 3 §13.1 / I-4). Citation re-verified exact 2026-09-06 (eighth issuance); symbol bound per the convention.

Row selected by the bearer token from the query string — `request.nextUrl.searchParams.get("token")` at `:12`, `.eq("token_hash", hashFormLinkToken(token.trim()))` at `:21`. Same `action_links` capability as /action/[token]. CITATION CORRECTED 2026-09-06 (eighth issuance): `:20` was the `.select(...)`, not the selector.

Row selected by the bearer token from the body — `.from("action_links")` at `:75`, `.eq("token_hash", hashFormLinkToken(token))` at `:77`, the token read at `:67` and documented at `:55` as the same raw `action_links.token` as the /action/[token] URL. Citation re-verified exact 2026-09-06 (eighth issuance); symbol bound per the convention.

Row selected by the bearer token — `.from("action_links")` at `:37`, `.eq("token_hash", hashFormLinkToken(token))` at `:39`; validity, consumption and expiry are checked before the write. Citation re-verified exact 2026-09-06 (eighth issuance); symbol bound per the convention.

Embed bootstrap. The gate is `buildPublicFormResolvePayload(createServiceRoleClient(), token, requestEmbedOrigin(request))` at `:24-28`, which calls `resolvePublicFormEmbedContext(supabase, token)` at `lib/public/forms/buildPublicFormResolvePayload.ts:59` and refuses on `!resolved.ok` at `:60`; it then enforces `isEmbedOriginAllowed` at `:70` (403 ORIGIN_FORBIDDEN). Every subsequent read is scoped to what the token resolved — the route's only caller input is the token itself (`plaintextToken(rawToken)` at `:22`). CITATION CORRECTED 2026-09-06 (eighth issuance), and SUBSTANTIVE: this entry named `resolvePublicFormEmbedContext` at `:31` as the gate, but that symbol is neither imported nor called in this route — `:31` is a `publicErr(...)` inside the failure branch. The gate moved down one level into a helper. The exception remains valid because the same function still runs, but the register was pointing a reviewer at a line that disproves it, and this is the second helper-refactor citation orphan in the register (see `tour-booking/[token]/resolve`), which is the 2026-08-06 record's warning that `a helper refactor is an exit from W-4's enforced predicate` showing up in the PROSE as well as in the check.

Creates a draft tied to the resolved public link — `resolvePublicFormEmbedContext(supabase, token)` at `:50` (imported `:20`). Creates only — no caller-supplied row selector. CITATION CORRECTED 2026-09-06 (eighth issuance): `:46`→`:50`.

Takes a caller-supplied submissionId, but binds it: `verifySubmissionBelongsToPublicEmbed(supabase, ctx, submissionId)` at `:58` (GET) and `:144` (PATCH) runs before the read/update, each preceded by `resolvePublicFormEmbedContext` at `:42` and `:97`. This is the subject-bound property I-4 requires. Both citations re-verified exact 2026-09-06 (eighth issuance) — the only entry in the register whose multi-line citation set survived re-measurement unchanged.

Same binding check — `verifySubmissionBelongsToPublicEmbed(supabase, ctx, submissionId)` at `:117`, after `resolvePublicFormEmbedContext` at `:75` — before the submit path executes. CITATION CORRECTED 2026-09-06 (eighth issuance): `:114`→`:117`.

Read-only participant view of their own Enrollment objective. `resolveParticipantEnrollmentFromToken(supabase, token)` is the gate: it calls the same `resolvePublicFormLinkByToken` the sibling routes use, then reaches the session by `started_via_public_link_id` and the journey by the D-95 `process_instance_id` anchor. Every read is scoped to what the token resolved — no caller-supplied row selector reaches a query, and the wire model withholds org, revision, requirement, session and item ids.

Same gate, and the write is doubly bound: the session is reached only through the token's own link, and the turn being answered is re-resolved server-side rather than accepted from the caller. The only mutations are `shared_values` and the D-99 confirmation map on that one session row, both keyed by a need the platform selected — the request body carries a value, never a target.

Same `resolveParticipantEnrollmentFromToken` gate as its siblings. The caller names a field id from the artifact under review, but the shared key that field writes to is resolved server-side from the session's PINNED form version (`sharedKeyForFieldId`), and an unbound field is refused with NOT_SHARED — so the only mutation is a `shared_values` merge on the token's own session row, and the request body carries a value, never a target.

Same gate, READ-ONLY. The request selects nothing: the token resolves the session, the session's D-94 pin selects the form version, the version's fidelity mapping selects the source document, and a sha256 pin refuses drifted bytes. The response is the participant's own filled document, rendered from the same value view the sibling routes serve — no caller-supplied row selector exists anywhere on the path.

Same gate. The body carries a PNG (magic-bytes verified, 300KB cap) and no target: the document row attaches to the session's D-95 anchor subject, resolved server-side from the token's own process instance. The only writes are one storage object and one `documents` row for that subject; the row id is returned so the Forms signature evidence can reference it, exactly as the operator-side drawn path expects.

Svix `new Webhook(secret).verify(...)` against `RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET` at `:110` (secret read `:95`, 503 if unset `:97`), and it returns 400 before `createAdminClient()` is constructed at `:132` — no statement reaches the database on an unsigned request, and the ordering that makes this true (`:110` < `:132`) was re-derived from the tree, not assumed. The handler documents at `:90` that session auth MUST NOT gate it. CITATIONS CORRECTED 2026-09-06 (eighth issuance): `:69`→`:110`, `:91`→`:132`. The security property is unchanged; both line numbers had drifted by roughly 40 lines, which is the largest drift in the register and the reason the ordering claim had to be re-checked rather than carried.

GET returning (id, name, slug) for active rows of the platform-global `verticals` table. No org-scoped or personal data, no caller-supplied selector, no write. RLS bypass discloses nothing tenant-specific.

Pricing/addon catalogs for the public booking UI. The org is pinned to `process.env.ALLOY_PUBLIC_ORG_ID` at `:26` — never caller-supplied — and the handler is read-only. Citation re-verified exact 2026-09-06 (eighth issuance); symbol bound per the convention.

Org pinned to `process.env.ALLOY_PUBLIC_ORG_ID` at `:17` and 500s without it at `:19`; `entityType` is validated against the fixed `allowed` array declared at `:32` and enforced at `:33-38` (400 otherwise), and reaches the query only as `.eq("entity_type", entityType)` at `:47`/`:55`. Read-only, returns only fields explicitly flagged for public booking. Citations re-verified exact 2026-09-06 (eighth issuance); symbols bound per the convention.

Unauthenticated vendor application intake. Org pinned to `process.env.ALLOY_PUBLIC_ORG_ID` at `:33` and 500s without it at `:35-37`. Creates only — it selects no existing row by a caller-supplied id. Citation re-verified exact 2026-09-06 (eighth issuance); symbol bound per the convention.

Recipient-initiated Email unsubscribe; public by necessity (an unsubscribe link that requires a login is not an unsubscribe link). EVERY target is a signed claim, not a caller-supplied selector: the Person, the organization and the single mutable category all come out of the HMAC-verified token (`verifyUnsubscribeToken`, `lib/communications/preferences/unsubscribeToken.ts:130-168`, signature checked constant-time at `:144` BEFORE expiry at `:165`), and `applyUnsubscribeToken` (`lib/communications/preferences/applyUnsubscribe.ts:50-68`) reads nothing from the request — it destructures the claims at `:59` and hands them to `performUnsubscribe` at `:61`, which re-checks the person↔org pair against the database at `:78-84`. The caller therefore supplies no value the mutation uses at all — strictly narrower than the enrollment-turn precedent, where the caller supplies a value but never a target. The token cannot switch categories (`c` is signed), cannot cross tenants (`o` is signed, and persons is re-checked on the pair), and the only reachable write is toState="opted_out" through the canonical persistCommunicationPreference authority.

Same gate as its siblings — `resolveParticipantEnrollmentFromToken(supabase, token)` at `:52` (imported `:26`) — and READ-ONLY. The request selects nothing: it is a GET whose only caller input is the token itself, and `resolveActiveArtifact` at `:59` (imported `:29`) takes the org and session from the resolved access, never from the request. Both citations re-verified exact 2026-09-06 (eighth issuance), a second time after the sixth issuance. It answers which document the participant is on and where it is signed, for both renderer engines.

Same gate — `resolveParticipantEnrollmentFromToken` at `:73`. The caller names a field id (`body.field_id` → `fieldId`, `:86`) and NOTHING else, and it is bound: `resolveParticipantUploadDestination` at `:110` reads the session's own D-94-pinned schema and refuses any id that is not an upload destination on THAT artifact. The doc_type comes from the schema (`destination.docType`, `:146`), never the caller, and the entity is the session's own child read from `process_instances.subject_id` at `:124-128` — the request cannot name an entity. Bytes are magic-sniffed against a PDF/PNG/JPEG allow-list (`sniff`, `:53`) under a 10MB cap (`MAX_BYTES`, `:36`, enforced at `:96`). CITATIONS CORRECTED 2026-09-06: all five line references were drifted and `uploadDestinationForField` had been renamed to `resolveParticipantUploadDestination`. Reported by the fifth issuance (2026-09-04) and again by the sixth; applied here on the third. The authorization model itself was re-verified against the tree and is unchanged — only the citations were wrong.

advisory_transitive_only.reason: Public inbound gutter-lead intake. Reaches a service client through `@/lib/supabase` helpers rather than importing a constructor, so it sits outside the enforced predicate. Creates only (contact upsert + opportunity create); marked LEGACY_COMPAT in its own header. Flagged for W-15.

Twilio status callback; delegates to `handleTwilioSmsStatus`, which holds the service client. Webhook model — signature verification lives in the helper, not the route, which is why the route itself shows no principal.
Per-tenant subaccount variant of the same handler and the same model.

Recipient-scoped capability token, not a session principal. The route no longer constructs a service client: `guardTourActionRoute` (imported `:4`, called `:45`) holds it and returns it only after `authorizeTourAction` verifies the token hash, the link↔invitation recipient binding, and the action kind. `requiredActions` is the route constant `REQUIRED_ACTIONS` (`:32-41`) — never request-supplied. CORRECTED 2026-08-06: that constant now lists every action kind, so the previous reason's claim that `[view_tour_slots, view_tour_details]` keeps a decline- or cancel-only token from reading context is NO LONGER TRUE. The widening is deliberate and argued in the route header (`:15-24`) — any credential on the same invitation may re-read what the invitation already disclosed to that same recipient — and the authorizer still proves recipient binding, expiry and revocation. Read-only; discloses labels and status, never a person, opportunity, process or household id. CITATIONS CORRECTED 2026-09-06: `guardTourActionRoute` `:39`→`:45`, `REQUIRED_ACTIONS` `:27-35`→`:32-41`, header `:18-25`→`:15-24`. Also substantive — the constant lists EIGHT kinds, not the seven this entry claimed; `confirm_attendance` was added by PR #416 and the 2026-08-06 correction was never updated to follow it.

Same guard-held client and same capability model. Route constant `[view_tour_slots, reschedule_tour, select_tour_slot]` (:26) — CORRECTED 2026-08-06: `select_tour_slot` was added to the constant and the previous reason still named only the first two. The authorized link scopes the availability read, and the guard rate-limits per token under the `slots` budget.

Same guard-held client and same capability model. Route constant `[decline_tour]` (:14). Single-use: `consumeTourAction` closes the credential with a conditional `UPDATE ... WHERE consumed_at IS NULL`. Writes only the invitation's own decline state.

Same guard-held client and same capability model. Route constant `[confirm_tour]` (:19). The booking id comes from the credential via `loadBoundBooking`, never from the request body, so no caller-supplied selector reaches the write.

Same guard-held client and same capability model. Route constant `[reschedule_tour]` (:24). Booking id is credential-bound via `loadBoundBooking`; the requested slot is revalidated against `computeAvailableTourSlots` before `rescheduleTourBooking` runs.

Same guard-held client and same capability model. Route constant `[cancel_tour]` (:16). Booking id is credential-bound via `loadBoundBooking`, and the cancel is single-use through `consumeTourAction`.

Recipient-scoped capability token, not a session principal. Same guard-held client and model as the other public tour routes: `guardTourActionRoute` holds the service client and returns it only after `authorizeTourAction` verifies the token hash, the link↔invitation recipient binding, and the action kind. Route constant `[view_tour_details]` (:26) — a read-only Manage credential, so the caller cannot mutate. It mints a single-use `cancel_tour` credential bound to the booking loaded from the credential via `loadBoundBooking`, never from the request; it performs no cancellation itself.

Same guard-held client and same capability model. Route constant `[select_tour_slot, view_tour_slots]` (:36). Commitment consumes the select action (or finds the sibling select link when the reusable view credential is presented); booking write is invitation-bound, never a caller-supplied booking id. Rate-limited inside `guardTourActionRoute` under the `book` budget.

Same guard-held client and same capability model. Route constant `[confirm_attendance]` (:14). Booking id is credential-bound via `loadBoundBooking`; attendance affirmation does not change booking status_key and is idempotent through `confirmTourAttendance`.

reviewed_note: 2026-08-27: enrollment-artifact and enrollment-upload added as reviewed exceptions after they failed the check on staging. Both models verified against the tree line-by-line rather than assumed: the gate call, the absence of any caller-supplied row selector on the artifact route, and on the upload route the field-id binding, the schema-owned doc_type and the session-owned subject. 2026-08-03: dropped stale book-v2 entries after routes were removed from the tree (lists may only shrink). 2026-08-04 re-review: all 17 remaining entries re-checked against the tree — every one still exists, still holds a service client, and still resolves no principal (asserted by the lock). Citations spot-verified line-by-line for the two subject-binding entries (:58/:144, :114) and the tour-booking token resolve (:30). The ratchet ceiling was tightened 26 → 17 to match the post-retirement floor. 2026-08-06 reopen re-execution: the lock was RED on this base — the advisory ratchet capped the set at 3 while 10 routes qualified. Root cause: the ceilings lived only in the lock, so an allow-list-only commit could grow a list with `prebuild` still green. The ceilings now sit in this file and the check enforces them, over AND under. All 15 exceptions re-checked; unresolved re-tightened 17 → 15. Every advisory `requiredActions` citation was re-verified against the tree and four were wrong: three drifted line numbers (`slots` :20→:26, `reschedule` :21→:24, `resolve` :16→:27-35) and one substantive — `resolve`'s reason claimed a two-action constant that now lists all seven kinds, so the property it asserted was false. Corrected in place rather than silently rewritten. 2026-08-14: staging prebuild RED after PR #416 — `book` no longer directly imports a service client (stale exception) while both `book` and new `confirm-attendance` are transitive-only via `guardTourActionRoute`. Moved `book` off exceptions onto advisory; listed `confirm-attendance`; re-tightened unresolved 15 → 14; raised advisory ceiling 10 → 12 with history.
